claims.text: High-entropy alloys currently have insufficient heat-transfer capability for use as intermediate materials in plasma-facing reactor components.
High-entropy alloys currently have insufficient structural integrity for use as intermediate materials in plasma-facing reactor components.
Plasma arc additive manufacturing combined with interface engineering can improve heat-transfer capability while preserving structural integrity.
Plasma arc additive manufacturing with interface engineering will modify the alloy's microstructure architecture.
The interface between an alloy and its substrate or coating plays a crucial role in determining overall material performance.
Engineering the interface can enhance the alloy's thermal conductivity.
Engineering the interface can enhance the alloy's mechanical properties.
Plasma arc additive manufacturing can reduce thermal and residual stresses and improve mechanical properties because it has relatively low heat input.
Arc additive manufacturing can produce directional solidification microstructures associated with improved strength in high-entropy alloys.
The intervention will improve heat-transfer capability relative to current intermediate-layer materials and designs.
The intervention will preserve structural integrity relative to current intermediate-layer materials and designs.
The predicted benefits will hold under high-temperature conditions.
The predicted benefits will hold under applied loading conditions.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires structural integrity to be preserved, whereas the falsification rule requires structural integrity to be significantly improved. Preservation and significant improvement are different criteria.

The stated baseline is current intermediate-layer materials and designs, but the experiment uses high-entropy alloys made by unspecified traditional methods as the control; these controls are not established as equivalent.
